steps.headline: Should the block change colour with the palette you are using?
steps.today: The block is painted the one colour, whichever palette you are on.
steps.problem: On the pale palette it almost disappears into the background behind it.
steps.proposal: Yes repaints it per palette; No leaves it the one colour it is today.

steps.headline: How many blocks should the strip hold at once?
steps.today: One block fills the strip, and a second one takes its place.
steps.problem: You lose sight of the first the moment a second one arrives.
steps.proposal: Let the strip hold more than one at a time.

options.label: One
options.summary: The strip stays as it is today.
pros: Nothing to take in but the one thing in front of you.
cons: The one you were reading vanishes when the next arrives.

options.label: Two
options.summary: The newest and the one before it.
pros: You keep the one you were reading while the next arrives.
cons: Each of the two is half as wide.

options.label: As many as fit
options.summary: The strip fills up and then starts dropping the oldest.
pros: Nothing is ever taken off the screen before you have read it.
cons: They get narrow fast, and the strip is busy.

steps.headline: A block you dismiss stays gone until you ask for it back.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: the alternative is something that comes back uninvited.
steps.notice: Nothing yet — this becomes a row of the contract.

steps.headline: Which of these should the strip be allowed to hold?
steps.today: The strip holds one thing, and the newest one replaces it.
steps.problem: Two of the things it could hold are useful at the same time.
steps.proposal: Tick every one worth letting in; ticking two means the strip holds both.

options.label: A line of text
pros: The cheapest of the three, and it never moves.

options.label: A count
pros: One number you can read without stopping.

options.label: A coloured dot
cons: Two dots side by side are hard to tell apart.

steps.prompt: What should the strip be called?
steps.headline: What should the strip under the message box be called?
steps.today: It has no name, so it gets described differently every time it comes up.
steps.problem: Nobody can ask for it by name, and two people describing it do not sound alike.
steps.proposal: Give it one name and use it in the app, the help pages and here.
